report.tagline: India's largest stock broker by active users, built to make mutual funds and stocks simple for first-time investors.
report.simpleSummary: Groww is an app where you can buy mutual funds, shares, gold and more with a few taps. Opening an account is free and done on your phone in minutes. It started with mutual funds for beginners, then added stocks, futures and options, and loans to buy shares. It earns a small fee each time you trade, plus interest on loans and money parked with it.

overview.whatItDoes: Groww lets Indians invest in mutual funds, stocks, IPOs, ETFs, gold, US stocks and futures and options from one app. It made account opening fully digital and the app very simple, which pulled in millions of first-time investors from small towns. Today it also lends money to buy shares (MTF), runs its own mutual fund house and offers wealth advice through Fisdom.
howItWorks: You download the app, enter PAN and Aadhaar, do a video KYC and get a demat account the same day, for free.
You can start a SIP in a direct mutual fund from ₹100 with no commission.
You can buy and sell shares and apply for IPOs with UPI; Groww charges a small flat fee per order.
Active traders use futures and options and the Groww terminal; Groww earns ₹20 per order.
Groww lends money to buy more shares (MTF) and charges interest, and earns interest on idle client money.
overview.valueProposition: Investing that feels as easy as online shopping: free account, clean screens, low fees and no pushy sales calls. For Groww, a huge base of young investors who start small and trade or invest more over time.

steps.detail: Watches a YouTube video on SIPs or gets a referral from a friend.
Enters PAN, Aadhaar and bank details, does KYC on the phone.
Filters by 'Popular' or 'Index funds' and reads simple risk labels.
Sets ₹1,000 a month with a UPI autopay mandate.
Checks portfolio value going up over months.
Buys a first share or applies for a hot IPO.
Buys and sells options on the option chain screen, ₹20 per order.
Watches profit and loss live and sets a stop loss.
Closes trades before market close and checks the day's charges.
Wants to buy ₹2 lakh of a stock but has ₹1 lakh.
Activates MTF and agrees to terms.
Pays ₹1 lakh, Groww funds the rest.
Interest is charged daily on the borrowed amount.
Sells shares or adds cash to close the loan.

businessModel.summary: Groww makes money mostly from trading fees, led by futures and options, plus interest on margin loans and idle client money, and fees from its own mutual fund house.

revenueStreams.detail: ₹20 per futures or options order, about 45% of income in Q2 FY27.
Small fee per share order, about 17% of income.
Interest on loans to buy shares, about 10% of income.
Interest earned on client money waiting in the account, about 8%.
Commodity trading fees, Groww Mutual Fund fees and Fisdom wealth fees.

businessModel.pricing: Account opening and maintenance: free. Direct mutual funds: no commission. Stocks: ₹20 or 0.1% of order value, whichever is lower (minimum ₹5). Futures and options: ₹20 per executed order. Plus government and exchange charges.
costDrivers: Marketing and brand campaigns to win new users
Tech and engineering to keep the app fast on busy days
Interest cost on money borrowed for MTF
businessModel.unitEconomics: A typical active trader placing 40 options orders a month pays about ₹800 a month in brokerage, nearly ₹10,000 a year. A SIP-only user pays nothing directly; Groww earns only small float income and the chance they trade later. With 2.4 crore transacting users and about ₹6,000 crore yearly revenue run rate, Groww earns roughly ₹2,500 per user per year on average, and about half of that is profit. CAC rose 73% in H1 FY26, so each new user takes longer to pay back.

howTheyGetUsers: Simple, free onboarding that friends recommend
Finance content on YouTube and Groww's own blog and social channels
IPO season, when millions open accounts to apply
Brand ads on TV and cricket
whatBringsUsersBack: Monthly SIP debits and portfolio checks
growth.moat: Groww's moat is scale and trust with beginners: it has the most active users of any Indian broker, a brand first-time investors know, and a habit loop from SIPs. Switching brokers means moving your demat holdings, which few people bother to do.

competitors.name: Zerodha
competitors.positioning: Bootstrapped low-cost broker loved by serious traders, with Kite and Coin.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Groww is simpler and aimed at beginners; Zerodha has deeper tools and the Varsity learning brand.

competitors.name: Angel One
competitors.positioning: Listed broker with a big franchise network in smaller towns.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Groww grew without agents, through app design alone.

competitors.name: Upstox
competitors.positioning: Low-cost broker backed by Tata and Ratan Tata's early bet.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Groww has more users and a stronger mutual fund base.

competitors.name: Paytm Money and PhonePe Share.Market
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Groww is a focused investing app with a clearer brand for investing.

northStar.metric: Monthly transacting users who hold investments with Groww
northStar.why: It shows people are actively putting money to work through Groww, which is the value it promises. Revenue follows when these users trade, borrow or grow their assets.

improvementIdeas.idea: A 'risk check' screen before a user's first options trade, showing SEBI data that most retail traders lose money
improvementIdeas.problem: Beginners lose money in options and blame the app; regulators are watching.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer heavy losses, less regulatory risk, more long-term trust.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of new options traders with losses above ₹50,000 in 90 days

improvementIdeas.idea: Goal-based investing: pick a goal like a home down payment, and Groww suggests a fund mix and SIP amount
improvementIdeas.problem: Beginners do not know what to buy or how much.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher SIP amounts and better retention.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Average SIP amount and SIP continuation rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Peak-day load protection with a status page and priority for exits
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Order failure rate on top 10 busiest days

improvementIdeas.problem: Users cannot reach a human for money problems.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Faster fixes, higher trust among bigger investors.

pmLessons: Simplicity can be the whole product edge: Groww won beginners by removing steps, not adding features.
Start with a low-risk entry product (SIPs) to build trust, then offer higher-value products (stocks, options, loans).
When most revenue comes from one product, regulation can hit hard, so diversify early.
Growth through design and word of mouth keeps CAC low and profit high.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow average assets per user on Groww?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users, look at SIP size, goal-based nudges, salary-day prompts, and track net money added.

interviewQuestions.question: SEBI tightens options rules again. What does Groww do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Estimate revenue at risk, push MTF, funds and wealth, and use the change to build trust with beginners.

interviewQuestions.question: Design onboarding for a first-time investor in a tier 3 town.
interviewQuestions.hint: Vernacular language, video KYC, ₹100 SIP, simple risk labels, and a clear first-week plan.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Groww's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare users, assets and revenue; pick one that reflects investor value, then break into drivers.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you compete with Zerodha for serious traders?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at tool gaps, terminal speed, pricing, and whether it is worth chasing vs serving beginners well.

assumptions: Revenue per user of about ₹2,500 a year is our estimate from quarterly revenue and transacting users.
